messages:
Marie: Heads up — docusaurus build failed on the migration guide after markdownlint autofix ran. Anchors are collapsing (links to in-page fragments 404).

docs-bot: CI failure detected: Docusaurus build error parsing anchor slugs in /docs/guides/migrations.md: line 134. Build log: https://ci.redwood.example/ab12cd (artifact attached)

Tony: I think markdownlint's rule removed the trailing colon in the heading so the slug changed. Example: `### Breaking changes: v2 -> v3` became `### Breaking changes v2 -> v3` which changes the generated id.

Samir: Ugh. Those subtle punctuation changes break a bunch of cross-page refs. Can we add explicit header ids for stable anchors? e.g.

Tony: ```
### Breaking changes: v2 -> v3 {#breaking-changes-v2-v3}
```

Olivia: We should be careful — we have both mkdocs and docusaurus pipelines for different zones of the site. Which renderer generated that page originally?

Marie: This page lives in the docs/ guides set which is now rendered by Docusaurus since the migration. The mkdocs->docusaurus conversion preserved text but relied on implicit slug rules — so yes, explicit ids are safer.

Samir: Quick regex I used to add ids to H2/H3 headings without an existing `{#...}`: 

`grep -nE "^(##|###) .+" docs/guides/*.md | sed -E "s/^(##+ )(.+)$/\1\2 {#\L\2}/"`

(then I ran a small sanitization step to remove spaces/punct for the id)

Tony: I opened a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 — backfilled explicit ids on 8 pages and added a note in CONTRIBUTING about heading punctuation.

Marie: Nice. Can you also add a markdownlint config tweak to turn off 'heading-style' autofix for the docs folder so future runs don't silently change headings?

Tony: Added in the PR: `.markdownlint.json` override for `docs/**` to disable the autofix rule. snippet:

```
{
  "docs/**": {
    "MD025": false
  }
}
```

Olivia: Ran `yarn docusaurus build` locally on Tony's branch — build succeeds and the anchor tests in our linkcheck job pass.

Samir: Cool — I'll merge once CI green. Thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

Marie: Thanks all. Filing a followup ticket to audit other pages for implicit-punctuation anchors so we don't see surprises in the next migration.

docs-bot: Linkcheck job passed for PR #482 — 0 broken fragments.
